_comment: Offline fixture for the web-highlights tool. Mirrors the shape we normalize Tavily search results into, so the same code path runs with or without a TAVILY_API_KEY. Image URLs are generated as local placeholder graphics at runtime (see web_server._placeholder_image) — nothing here hotlinks the real web.

highlights.title: What to order
highlights.snippet: Regulars point to the house specials and the chef's tasting selection as the dishes worth building a meal around. Ask your server what came in fresh that day.

highlights.title: Osteria Midtown — a Midtown classic for sharing
highlights.snippet: The kitchen built its reputation on hand-rolled pasta: the cacio e pepe arrives finished tableside, and the family-style antipasti board is the thing to start with when there are four of you.

highlights.title: Menu — Osteria Midtown
highlights.snippet: Signature plates include cacio e pepe, veal osso buco, and a rotating seasonal risotto. Large tables are steered toward the sharing platters.

highlights.title: Trattoria del Sole — Sicilian wine and slow cooking
highlights.snippet: A sommelier-led regional wine list is the draw here, paired with a short menu of Sicilian braises. The pistachio-crusted swordfish is the dish people come back for.

highlights.title: Nonna's Gluten-Free Kitchen — a fully celiac-safe kitchen
highlights.snippet: Everything leaving this kitchen is gluten-free, so there is no cross-contamination question to ask. The tasting flight of small plates is how most first-timers order.

highlights.title: Menu — Nonna's Gluten-Free Kitchen
highlights.snippet: Gluten-free tasting flight, wood-fired margherita on a house GF base, and a flourless chocolate torte that regulars call the best in the neighbourhood.

highlights.title: Le Petit Bistro — candlelit and unhurried
highlights.snippet: A small room built for two-tops. The dégustation menu changes weekly; the duck confit and the tarte tatin are the fixtures nobody will let them take off.

highlights.title: Sakura Omakase — sit at the counter
highlights.snippet: Omakase only, twelve to sixteen courses depending on the day's fish. The counter seats are the experience; tables miss half of it.

highlights.title: Taqueria La Luz — late-night al pastor
highlights.snippet: The trompo runs all evening and the al pastor tacos are the reason for the queue. Order the quesabirria too, and eat standing up if you have to.

highlights.title: Spice Route — regional Indian, properly spiced
highlights.snippet: They will ask how hot you want it and they mean it. The vegetarian thali is the best way to sample the range, and the dal makhani is cooked overnight.

highlights.title: The Prime Cut — dry-aged and quiet enough to talk
highlights.snippet: A steakhouse built for business dinners: dry-aged ribeye, a serious cellar, and booths spaced far enough apart to hold a conversation.

highlights.title: Bangkok Orchid — the vegan side of the menu is not an afterthought
highlights.snippet: Half the menu can be made vegan without losing the fish-sauce depth, which is rare. The green curry and the som tam are where to start.

highlights.title: Verdant — vegetables treated like the main event
highlights.snippet: A seasonal plant-based tasting menu that changes with what's good that month. The charred hispi cabbage has been on since opening because guests revolt when it isn't.
